newsitem.title: CANADA: Air Canada union authorizes strike action.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada union authorizes strike action.

text.p: Members of Canadian Auto Workers union local 2213 representing 3,500 Air Canada sales and service agents voted 91 percent in favor of strike action to press for a new equitable collective agreement, the union said on Wednesday.
More than 70 percent of members voted, the CAW said.

"Our members have sent a clear message to Air Canada that they support their bargaining committee and they demand progress this year," said Cheryl Kryzaniwsky, president of local 2213, in a statement.
Negotiations between the carrier and union broke off on September 28 after more than four weeks of talks in which Air Canada refused to make an economic offer to the membership, the union said.

The CAW said its main issues were wages, benefits and job security. It charged that Air Canada was demanding the unlimited use of temporary workers and increased flexibility in the employment of workers.
"Air Canada's concessionary demands are unacceptable to our members," said Tom Freeman, chairman of the union bargaining committee.
"These concessionary demands mean deteriorating working conditions for all of our members," he said.
Conciliation in the contract dispute is scheduled for October 28-29. After the conciliation process, members would be in a legal strike position in time for Christmas, the CAW said.
The 3,500 Air Canada employees represented by Local 2213 are customer sales and service agents who work at airports, in Aeroplan and at reservations and ticket offices across Canada.
